trivial_change_silence.notes: Skill correctly identified this as a trivial change that would generate zero substantive review comments. The only reviews were a Gemini bot summary (COMMENTED) and a one-line APPROVED from a maintainer ('Thanks for the cleanup!'). No inline code comments were left. The skill prevented us from manufacturing false nit-picks on clean dead code removal.

key_insight: The trivial_change_silence skill works well for pure dead code removal by a high-authority author. The combination of (1) subtractive-only change, (2) author is the upstream library maintainer, and (3) clear PR description explaining why the code is dead, produces a frictionless merge with zero substantive review comments.
hypothesis: No correction needed — prediction was fully correct. The trivial_change_silence skill accurately identified the pattern: small subtractive change + high author authority + clear justification = clean merge with no review friction. The 0.95 confidence was appropriately calibrated (could even have been higher). One reinforcement: bot-generated reviews (Gemini code assist) should not count as substantive human review comments — they are automated summaries and don't indicate reviewer concern.
